To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The annual modulation effect observed in the DAMA/Na1 and DAMA/LIBRAs data has been found to be present in all the phases of the experiment.

the annual modulation of the rate of nuclear recoils in the NaI(Tl) detectors of the DAMA/LIBR experiment, accumulated over 13 annual periods of data taking, is compatible with the expected signature from Dark Matter WIMP annual modulation signal, and that the evidence is model independent.

DAMA/LIBRAnoticeably detects annual modulation in the NaI(Tl) event rate with a modulation amplitude of (0.0110±0.0011) cpd/kgkeV at 8.2 σ C.L. and that the data are in agreement with the expected signature from DM particles in the Galactic Halo.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the investigation of DM particles in our Galaxy, by exploiting the model-independent DM annual modulation signature, with the present DAMA/LI- BRA set up, and with the development of new techniques for DM searches.
the search for DM particles, which are expected to be weakly interacting, massive particles (WIMPs).
the investigation of Dark Mater particles by exploiting the model in- dependent DM annual modulation signature, as predicted in several theories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the DAMA/LIBRAs data are fully compatible with those of other DM experiments, and the DAMA annual modulation result is not in contradiction with the other experiments results, if one takes into account the different experimental approaches, the different nature of the target, the different exposure and the different sensitivity to the DM particle model.
, in view of all experimental data and of the results of the DAMA/LIBRAs experiment in particular, the DM particle interpretation of the DAMA annual modulation effect is the most solid one.

, in the absence of systematical errors, the DAMA/Na I and DAMA/LIB- RA results are in agreement with the hypothesis of the presence of particles in the gal-actic halo, with a DM particle annual modulation signal at high C.L.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DAMA is the first experiment that has provided evidence of DM particles in nature.
we have a model independent evidence for the presence of DM in the galactic halos.
the model independent DM evidence is still standing and is now confirmed by other experiments, in spite of the fact that some of them have not yet reached the sensitivity required to confirm it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DAMA/LIBR A has provided the first evidence of DM particles in our galactic halo, which is model independent, robust and not affected by the presence of any known background.

the DAMA/LIB- RA annual modulation results are compatible with the presence of a DM component in the galactic halos and they cannot be ascribed to known sources of seasonal modulations, such as those related to the atmospheric conditions and/or the seasonal changes of the environmental radioactivity, as recently claimed by some authors.
the DAMA/LIBR A annual modulation results are in agreement with the galactic DM model, and that they are not compatible with the null results of any other experiments.
